title: Implicit user feedback and engagement signals
summary: Confirmed in the saved records: in the US v. Google trial, Nayak said Navboost is a factor but not the only one and agreed that 'user feedback' in a document meant click data; Lehman said user data is widely used in Search and that Navboost is a big table, not machine learning. Google also says it reviews click metrics in live experiments. Not confirmed in the saved sources: dwell time, pogo-sticking, or any claim that one page's click-through rate lifts that page's ranking. Treat those as hypotheses.
actions: Separate what testimony confirms (clicks and user data are used) from what it does not (dwell time, pogo-sticking, per-page CTR effects).
Practitioner advice (not from a saved source): diagnose traffic drops with query-level click data before blaming engagement.
Practitioner advice (not from a saved source): be wary of click manipulation or widgets sold on unconfirmed claims.

myths.myth: Dwell time and pogo-sticking are confirmed ranking signals.
myths.correction: Not confirmed in the saved sources: none of the saved passages mention them.

myths.myth: Navboost is the only thing that matters.
myths.correction: Nayak said it is certainly a factor, but not the only factor by any means.

items.prompt: In Pandu Nayak's trial testimony, 'Glue' is another name for which system? One word.
items.explanation: Nayak said Glue is just another name for navboost that includes all of the other features on the page.

items.prompt: In his trial testimony, how did Nayak describe Navboost's role among ranking factors?
options: A. The sole ranking factor
B. Used only for ads
C. A system Google denied having
D. One factor, not the only one
items.explanation: Correct: he said it is certainly a factor but not the only factor by any means. Wrong: 'The sole ranking factor' - he said the opposite. 'Used only for ads' - not in the testimony. 'A system Google denied having' - he described it.

items.prompt: True or false: Google engineer Eric Lehman testified that Navboost is not a machine learning system, just a big table.
items.explanation: The Day 7 transcript has Lehman saying Navboost is not a machine learning system and is just a big table.

items.prompt: Google's 'Rigorous testing' page says it reviews metrics such as what people click on in live traffic experiments. What does that page support?
options: A. Your page's CTR is a confirmed ranking factor
B. Google uses click metrics to judge changes
C. Dwell time is a confirmed ranking signal here
D. Google does not run live experiments at all
items.explanation: Correct: it says Google evaluates changes to Search using aggregate metrics from real-user experiments. Wrong: 'Your page's click-through rate is a confirmed ranking factor' - the page describes evaluating changes, not per-page ranking. 'Dwell time is confirmed' - the page mentions time to click, not dwell. 'Experiments are never run' - it says they are.

items.prompt: True or false: the saved trial passages confirm that dwell time and pogo-sticking are ranking signals.
items.explanation: Not found in the saved sources: the saved witness answers and exhibit passages mention clicks and user data, and none of the saved passages mention dwell time or pogo-sticking. That is an absence in what was saved, not proof Google does not use them.

items.prompt: Which statement is NOT supported by the saved sources?
options: A. Nayak said Navboost is not the only factor
B. Nayak agreed 'user feedback' in a document meant click data
C. Google confirmed pogo-sticking demotes pages
D. Lehman said user data is widely used within Search
items.explanation: Correct answer C: no saved source says pogo-sticking demotes a page. Supported: A (Nayak: Navboost is a factor, not the only one), B (Nayak confirmed user feedback means click data), D (Lehman: user data is widely used within Search).

items.prompt: A client asks what you can honestly tell them about clicks and rankings. Choose the strongest supported statement.
options: A. Dwell time is confirmed to lift rankings
B. Click data is used; page-level effects unproven
C. Rewriting titles will raise your rankings reliably
D. Google does not use click data in any way
items.explanation: Correct: it uses only what the record shows (Nayak agreed user feedback means click data; Lehman said user data is widely used). Wrong: A claims dwell time is confirmed; C claims title changes will raise rankings, which no source supports; D denies any use of clicks, contradicted by the testimony.

items.prompt: A summary says: (1) Nayak said Navboost is a factor but not the only one. (2) Lehman called it a big table, not a machine learning system. (3) Therefore Navboost is all that matters for rankings. Which step is the error?
options: A. Step 1
B. Step 2
C. Step 3
D. No step is an error
items.explanation: Step 3 contradicts step 1, since Nayak said it is not the only factor. Steps 1 and 2 restate the testimony.

items.prompt: Case file (hypothetical site, Brightfield Garden Supply): traffic fell after a redesign. A consultant says pogo-sticking caused it and proposes a time-on-page widget to fix it. Evidence: (1) the saved witness answers discuss click data and user data (Nayak agreed 'user feedback' in a document meant click data; Lehman said user data is widely used within Search), and none of the saved passages mention dwell time or pogo-sticking; (2) Nayak said Navboost is a factor, not the only one; (3) no data in hand shows which queries lost clicks. Which action is best?
options: A. Find which queries lost clicks first
B. Install the widget to raise time on page
C. Conclude the drop cannot be investigated
D. Blame Navboost for the drop
items.explanation: Correct: treat pogo-sticking as an untested hypothesis, find which queries lost clicks, and compare against what ranks. Wrong: 'Install the widget' - acts on an unconfirmed cause. 'Assume nothing can be done' - ignores Search Console data. 'Blame Navboost' - the record does not say that.

items.prompt: Case file (hypothetical site, Cedar Cabinets): the owner reads that Google reviews click metrics and concludes 'raising our CTR will raise our rankings'. Evidence: (1) Google's Rigorous testing page says it reviews metrics such as what people click on in live experiments; (2) the same page describes evaluating changes for everyone, not individual pages; (3) at trial Nayak agreed that 'user feedback' in a document means click data, and said Navboost is not the only factor. Which interpretation is best?
options: A. Proven: higher CTR raises that page's rank
B. Clicks are never used by Google at all
C. Only dwell time matters for rankings
D. Clicks are used; page effect unconfirmed
items.explanation: Correct: Google uses click metrics to evaluate changes, and Nayak agreed a document's 'user feedback' meant click data, but no saved source says one page's CTR lifts its own ranking. Wrong: 'Proven: higher CTR raises that page's rank' - overreads. 'Clicks are never used by Google at all' - contradicted by the testimony and Google's testing page. 'Only dwell time matters for rankings' - unsupported.
